title: Inter-region failover priority saturation causing unexpected dedicated capacity shortfall
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers observed sustained 5–30s tail latency increases and a spike in 429s during an inter-region failover window. Investigation shows dedicated reserved pools dropped effective headroom unexpectedly and the autoscaler scaled down while tenant requests were still warming, causing cascade cold-starts and partial tenant outages. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate mitigations, and a targeted bugfix for the autoscaler/allocator interaction during cross-region failover events.

Scope: Hosted/Dedicated environments impacted where reserved-pool failover (AZ->AZ or region->region) triggered a rapid rebalancing of tenant allocations. Private deployments that use the same autoscaler control plane are potentially affected if they opt into multi-region failover.

Observed timeline (short):
- 2025-02-18 02:13 UTC: Inter-region failover triggered for cloud provider maintenance in eu-west causing a rapid migration of several replica sets.
- 02:16 UTC: Headroom predictor reported sudden drop in warm slots for several reserved pools.
- 02:17-02:21 UTC: Autoscaler enacted a scale-down due to aggregate headroom metric below threshold.
- 02:22 UTC: Tenant requests began hitting cold pools; KV cache evictions increased memory churn and eviction-driven restarts for some warm workers.
- 02:25–03:05 UTC: Customer-facing error rates increased; on-call applied emergency slow-roll fallback to larger, cheaper model variant and enabled burst-fallback routing for top-tier tenants.

Impact: Several mid-market customers (3 confirmed) experienced degraded throughput and elevated latencies for ~40 minutes. One enterprise customer reported timeouts for synchronous RPCs and filed an escalation. Billing and cost impact: no billing discrepancy, but SLA credits being evaluated.

Repro steps:
1) Simulate rapid AZ->AZ replica move in a cluster with mixed tenant cardinality (1 large tenant + many small tenants).
2) Force rebalancer to preemptively drain a subset of warm nodes and observe headroom predictor smoothing window.
3) Observe autoscaler reaction when headroom integrates across regions without applying failover hysteresis.
4) Confirm KV cache eviction churn increases memory pressure on remaining warm instances.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Failover rebalancer aggressively relocated replica sets; headroom predictor aggregated short-window signals and incorrectly reported sustained low warm slots because it did not account for inflight reallocation in the other region.
- Autoscaler lacked a failover-aware hysteresis: it considered aggregated headroom only and allowed scale-down without a safe hold period for recently drained pools.
- KV cache eviction increased memory churn on the remaining nodes which caused transient failures that the autoscaler interpreted as idle capacity, compounding the scale-down decision.
- Telemetry aggregation bug: headroom metric used a 1m non-overlapping bucket which masked rapid recoveries, making transient dips look persistent to the controller.

Immediate mitigations applied (rollbackable hotfixes):
- Hotpatch deployed at 2025-02-18 03:40 UTC: increased autoscaler min_headroom_multiplier for affected pools to 1.5 and disabled scale-down for 10m after any failover signal. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9038)
- Emergency runbook executed: enable burst-fallback routing to compatible model variants and route critical tenants to dedicated warmbackups.
- Added synthetic Canary that simulates warmup under failover to surface regressions in future windows.

Proposed long-term fix (workstreams):
- Autoscaler: introduce failover-aware hysteresis (hold window + safe_headroom reservation) so scale-downs do not run while rebalancer is converging. (owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Headroom predictor: switch to overlapping sliding windows (15s stride, 60s window) and expose raw per-region signals to the autoscaler for decision-making. (owner: Priya Singh)
- Allocator/Lease protocol: mark leases that are in-migration or recently preempted as protected for a cooldown duration to preserve warm slots. (owner: Marco Diaz)
- KV cache: add an eviction backoff to avoid synchronized cache flushes during node churn and monitor memory_pressure events. (owner: Sarah Kim)
- Telemetry: fix aggregation bug and add a failover event flag that the autoscaler can subscribe to. (owner: Observability team)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Autoscaler retains sufficient headroom (>= configured safe_headroom) during simulated failover tests with no customer-facing request failures.
2) New sliding-window headroom metrics show <5% false-positive scale-downs in synthetic failover tests.
3) Post-deploy canary (3 tenants of varying sizes) run for 72h with no cold-start cascade triggered by a controlled failover.
4) Dashboards show no unexplained 429 spike in next production failover.
5) Documentation and runbook updated and reviewed by on-call and SRE.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (hotfix): short hold window and min_headroom multiplier (already rolled out to eu-west and us-central). Phase 2 (target runtime-1.19): implement failover-aware hysteresis and sliding-window headroom; roll out to one region as canary for 72h. Phase 3: global rollout with monitoring guardrails and automatic rollback on >5% increase in SLA errors.
Rollback plan: revert runtime PR or flip runtime feature flag to 'failover-protection: off' and re-enable pre-existing autoscaler behavior.
Communication: notify affected customers via incident comms and follow-up with postmortem and remediation ETA.
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboards created: 'failover_headroom_viz', 'autoscaler_decision_log', 'kv_eviction_churn' and 'tenant_coldstart_spike'. Alerts: headroom_drop_without-failover_flag > 5m, autoscaler_scale_down_during_failover_flag, kv_eviction_rate_above_critical. Synthetic canary alert: canary_tail_latency > 2x baseline for 15m. Links: https://grafana.redwood-inference.net/d/failover_headroom, https://grafana.redwood-inference.net/d/kv_eviction_churn
runbook_steps: If customers report elevated latencies during a failover window: 1) Check 'failover' flag events and autoscaler decision log; 2) Temporarily set pool min_headroom_multiplier to 2.0 for affected pool; 3) Enable burst-fallback routing for top-tier tenants; 4) If memory churn present, increase node eviction_threshold and drain affected nodes gracefully; 5) Notify customers and open escalation channel.
comments: 2025-02-18 04:05 UTC — Aisha Patel: Initial hotpatch applied; customers on the escalation list acknowledged receipt of mitigation comms. Need to verify synthetic canary behavior in next scheduled window.

2025-02-19 09:12 UTC — Priya Singh: Headroom predictor prototype using overlapping sliding windows shows promising reduction in false positives in local tests (see gsheet results). Planning integration test with allocator team.

2025-02-20 14:30 UTC — Marco Diaz: Lease-protection design doc uploaded (GDrive): https://drive.google.com/lease-protection-design. Edge-case: long-lived leases that are intentionally drained by ops require an opt-out tag.
2025-02-21 18:41 UTC — Liam O'Connor: Implemented temporary autoscaler guard to ignore scale-down if a failover event was observed in last 10m. Deployed to eu-west; monitoring green so far.
2025-02-22 11:02 UTC — Sarah Kim: KV cache eviction backoff PR is ready for review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9105). Needs perf bench run before staging rollout.
follow_up_tasks: Add per-tenant warmup telemetry to reduce aggregate signal collisions
Run cross-region canary with 5 controlled failovers over 7 days
Update customer-facing incident FAQ and SLA communication template
notes: This ticket differs from prior burst-accounting incidents: root cause combines rebalancer-triggered churn + telemetry aggregation timing plus KV eviction feedback loop. Prior fixes addressed pure accounting/leak issues; this requires coordination between autoscaler, allocator, and cache subsystems.
